UniProtKB annotates residues 745-1027 of O00329 as Domain: PI3K/PI4K catalytic; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in manual assertion.
Dornan et al. report that the APDS1 p110delta mutations N334K, E525K and E1021K mimic the activation mechanisms previously found for oncogenic mutations in p110alpha.
InterPro annotates residues 676-1042 of O00329 as domain: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta, catalytic domain; evidence: match to sequence model evidence used in automatic assertion.

Using biochemical assays and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, Dornan et al. examined the molecular mechanism of activation of APDS mutations, and all APDS mutations tested were potently inhibited by idelalisib.

E5 and E9 tie APDS1 p110delta mutations to oncogenic p110alpha activation, which works through membrane binding. Weaknesses: E2 describes a gain of function, not the loss of function in the task premise (E13 also says gain). G1 leaves residue position unconfirmed and G5 means no mutant structure exists, so this is untested. Missing: a residue-level structural placement of E1021 and a membrane-binding assay for E1021K.

payload.statement: E1021 forms part of the interface with the p85 regulatory subunit; the charge reversal weakens the p85 (iSH2) restraint on p110delta, so the catalytic subunit is released from inhibition and becomes constitutively active.
payload.would_refute: In p110delta–p85 complex structures or docking models, residue 1021 has no atom within contact distance of the p85 regulatory subunit, and E→K leaves the predicted p85 binding energy unchanged or stronger.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: E19 confirms that PIK3CD is a heterodimer with p85, and E9 shows that p85 mutations activate p110delta strongly. It ranks below ligand_binding because no record item places E1021 at the p85 interface, and E5 concerns oncogenic activation in general rather than this residue. payload.statement: The charge reversal breaks an intramolecular salt bridge or contact between the 1008–1031 helix and the adjacent domain of the same p110delta chain, destabilising the autoinhibited conformation and shifting the catalytic domain toward the active state.
payload.would_refute: In the AlphaFold model and the 20 experimental structures, residue 1021 makes no side-chain contact with another domain of the same chain (no partner atom within about 4 Å), and molecular dynamics of wild type versus E1021K shows no change in the interdomain distance or helix position.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The helix at 1008–1031 (E3) sits in a well-predicted region (E17, mean pLDDT 87.94). Pathogenicity scores (E8 0.975, E14 0.681) and conservation (E10 0.918) show the residue matters, but none of them says where it contacts the chain. An interdomain contact is possible and consistent with the p110alpha analogy in E5, but it is the least supported of the three because the record contains no contact data. It also conflicts with the loss-of-function premise, since this mechanism would more naturally produce gain of function. Missing: the contact map for residue 1021 (G1, G5), and a stability calculation for E1021K.

payload.text:
## Question
What mechanism best explains the reported loss of function of PIK3CD-p.Glu1021Lys (O00329), and what does it point to? The task states loss of function, but the record calls E1021K a gain of function [E2], so this direction conflict is not resolved (see Uncertainty).

## Evidence
ClinVar classifies the variant as pathogenic for immunodeficiency 14 [E1]. UniProt records it as a gain of function with enhanced membrane association and kinase activity [E2]. Dornan et al. report that it mimics activation mechanisms of oncogenic p110alpha mutations [E5]. Residues 1008-1031 are annotated as a helix [E3]. AlphaMissense (0.9748) [E8] and EVE (0.681) [E14] are computational predictions, not validated. No functional assay covers residue 1021 [G4], no experimental structure carries the substitution [G5], and the size of the effect is not established [G2].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
Three agent-generated hypotheses were formed: H1, ligand binding through membrane association [H1]; H2, release of p85 restraint [H2]; and H3, breaking of an intramolecular contact [H3]. H1 ranked first on the starting evidence [H1].

## Tests considered and the choice
Round 1: the planner chose T1 (structural context) and rejected T2, T3 and T4 [T1]. H1 was favoured before the test. Round 2 was reopened because T1 weakened H1. The planner chose T2 (ligand contact) and rejected T3 and T4. T4 was blocked by the provider and needed approval [T2].

## Result
T1: residue 1021 lines none of 22 P2Rank pockets but lies in one ProtVar predicted pocket with buriedness 0.82 [T1, E20, E21]. It is in no predicted protein-protein interface [E22]. T2: no non-solvent ligand lies within 4.5 Å of residue 1021 across 20 experimental structures [T2, E23]. Both results weakened H1 and H2; H3 was unchanged [T1, T2].

## Updated decision
H1 was favoured before the test and after both rounds [H1]. It was weakened but not refuted, so the decision did not change. The reopening occurred once [T2].

## Candidates
The lab's rule maps increased activity to reducing it, pointing at the p110delta catalytic subunit's ATP-binding pocket [R1]. The translator proposed three candidates for this direction. Safety cleared none and rejected all three, because no cited record supports the gain-of-function premise [G6]. The direction filter removed no rows; the three rows were removed by the safety block. No candidate was recorded. Any molecule would be a Helix hypothesis, not a recommendation.

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
The gain-versus-loss conflict is unresolved [E2, E13, G6]. The H1 membrane-facing premise is untested: T2 used soluble ATP-site ligands, not membrane lipids [T2]. T1 and T2 are computational or structure-database checks, not measurements. No assay has measured E1021K activity or membrane binding [G2]. The structural p85 interface check was null, which is not a confirmed absence [T1].

## Next experiment
Test H1 against PIP2 head-group contact and the membrane-facing electrostatic potential, wild type versus E1021K, on AF-O00329-F1 [H1, T2]. This is the open would-refute test for H1. It needs no approval and no external provider.
